steps.text: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir in the onion, and cook until almost tender. Stir in rice, and continue cooking until coated with oil. When onion is tender and rice begins to brown lightly, season with pepper, and pour in the broth. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Onion Rice
raw_recipe.description: Simple and versatile rice side dish that everyone loves!
raw_recipe.name: Onion Rice

recipeInstructions.text: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir in the onion, and cook until almost tender. Stir in rice, and continue cooking until coated with oil. When onion is tender and rice begins to brown lightly, season with pepper, and pour in the broth. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 20 minutes.

review.reviewBody: As I started to make this recipe I realized I didn't have onions on hand. After looking through the cupboard, I narrowed down the choices to an envelope of Liptons dried soup mix and a can of French Onion Soup. FOS won out.... Pureed the onions in the soup and then added chicken broth to make up the difference in liquid. Wonderful with substitutions ~

READER BEWARE---I changed some things. I used microwave brown rice . I sauteed 1/3 of an red onion in a sauce pan with butter and then added the cooked rice to which i added some chicken broth to moisten it up and fresh parsley to finish. It looked and tasted great.

As is, it was just okay. I made some changes and then everyone seemed to like it a lot. I sauteed white onion, celery (leafy greens and all) and garlic in butter. Then toasted the rice and I always use chicken base (btb) in lieu of chicken broth. After it was finished, I added a good handful of thinly sliced almonds for a little crunch.

We love this rice!! There are so many adjustments you can use. I use olive oil and butter to cook the onion, but use a brown onion. When adding the rice, I put in some chopped fresh parsley for nice color. I use one cup chicken broth and one cup water with a dissolved chicken bullion cube which adds perfect flavor and salt amount. I don’t add the heavy pepper or any extra salt. I tried the red onion which was okay, it wasn’t as flavorful as the brown onion. We like this the next night too!!

Yummy.. Made too much and excited for the leftovers. Used jasmine rice and chicken stock. Toasted the rice with a half of very finely chopped red onion and half packet of onion soup mix. Then added all ingredients to rice cooker, the house smelled divine. Tasted good too. No need to add salt as well!

My daughter who doesn't like onions liked this. I did use instant rice and it turned out great (needed it done quicker). I didn't fry the rice- after sauteing the onion I added the broth, got it to boil then added the rice, took it off the heat and covered it. I also used sweet white onion as I was worried the red onion might not look as nice. Very good!!

This is a wonderful easy recipe. I used Carolina Gold Rice and added broccoli when it was done. You can add chicken too for a complete meal. Budget friendly too. Next time I will add some sautéed mushrooms for a mushroom version. I do not think you will be disappointed. My whole family loved it!
This is a good basic recipe. I add minced garlic. I throw mine in the rice cooker after browning then add chicken broth.

This was a mild flavored rice that would be a great side dish with just about anything. I only used a third of a large Texas sweet onion and used a little more oil than called for because as soon as the onion was translucent I added the dry rice in and cooked it until it was starting to turn light golden, then I added a dab of minced garlic stirred it in and cooked for less than a minute and finally added in the broth. I forgot the black pepper but it didn't need it after all. Definitely a wonderful rice recipe and I will be making this again. Thanks Denyse!
Love the recipe, quick and easy and tastes great. I did cut down on the pepper though. I used 1/2 tsp and it was plenty for my taste.

I used a vidalia onion and sauteed it in butter and olive oil. I added rice and garlic powder and sauteed a bit longer. I used beef broth (it was all I had thawed). The flavors were outstanding. My husband, who is not a huge fan of rice, had three servings. My small kids loved it as well. I will definitely be making this again!
Loved it. I'm a big onion lover so I fixed this with BBQ bacon wrapped chicken and green beans.

This was simple, straight forward, and good. It's basic enough that it pairs well with any protein. I made as directed but I'd cut back on the black pepper next time. I did like the color the red onion added but any onion you have on hand would work.
Best dish ever !!!❤️😍

I highly suggest spanish/yellow onion rather than red, and i don't add the pepper, but rather a little salt after cooking (i use low-sodium broth). but, this is a good, classic side dish! goes great with chicken schnitzel!
Little heavy on the pepper and short on the broth. Otherwise perfect.
Added half a teaspoon of salt and a quarter teaspoon of pepper.
Made this, using water in place of chicken broth and added more lemon juice. Was still flavourful, would make again!
A welcomed change from plain steamed rice. Turned out nice and fluffy.
We all liked it but it was a tiny bit flat, next time I plan to add sauteed garlic and a touch of salt.
